settings.definition_quote: We denote by $D\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ the \textit{finite} arm set ... we further assume that $D$ spans $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\|x\|_2\leq 1$ ... we assume $\norm{\theta_t}_2 \le 1$ ... In this work, we consider the non-oblivious adversary

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandits with corruption level C
settings.definition_quote: For the corrupted stochastic environment, it is also satisfied that $\theta_t=\theta$ for some \textit{unknown} $\theta$, but the learner now receives loss $\ell_t(x_t)=\left\langle x_t,\theta \right\rangle+\epsilon_t\left(x_t\right)+c_t$, where $c_t$ is the corrupted value chosen by the adversary ... let $C=\sum_{t=1}^T|c_t|$ be the corruption level

source.label: thm:thmregret
source.quote: In the adversarial environment, regret can be upper bounded by R(T) \le O\bracket{\sqrt{dT\ln T \ln(|D|T)}}

results.notes: K = |D|. Regret is expected pseudo-regret per the paper's definition. Learning rate uses ln T so horizon known.

source.label: thm:thmregret
source.quote: In the stochastic environment with corruption level $C$, the regret can be bounded by R(T) \le O \bracket{\frac{ d\ln T \ln (|D|T) }{ \Delta_{\min}} + \sqrt{\frac{Cd\ln T \ln (|D|T)}{\Delta_{\min}}}  }

results.notes: C=0 gives the stochastic result. Proof goes via the (Delta,C,T) self-bounding constraint; corruption c_t arbitrary (not linear). Delta_min is min gap over suboptimal arms.
